title: The VPN update
setting: Fictional Inland State University, 2026-10-28. All people, hosts, messages, logs and flows are invented for practice. Addresses use reserved example ranges.

stages.title: 1. Email triage
stages.intro: Read the message and authentication results. Record the attachment for the endpoint pivot.
evidence: E01 | 2026-10-28 09:02 UTC | To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@isu.example.org> | From: IT Service Desk <help@isu-support.example.com> | Subject: Required VPN certificate update
E02 | Reply-To: service@isu-support.example.com | Return-Path: bounce@isu-support.example.com | Message-ID: <4621@isu-support.example.com>
E03 | Authentication-Results: spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=isu-support.example.com; dkim=pass header.d=isu-support.example.com; dmarc=pass header.from=isu-support.example.com
E04 | Body: “Install the attached certificate updater before noon to keep campus VPN access.” Attachment: VPN-Cert-Update.zip
E05 | Gateway extraction: VPN-Cert-Update.zip contains VPN-Cert-Update.js; SHA-256 (script) = 6e9e6b8ffb8c29a258ba2e37df1461fa896675e682d593af13b6d4b579207a92
E06 | Directory note: official IT notices use isu.example.org; isu-support.example.com is an unrelated lookalike example domain.

questions.prompt: Who was targeted? Enter the mailbox.
questions.hint: Read the To header in E01.
questions.timeline: 09:02 UTC — phishing email sent to maya.chen@isu.example.org.

questions.hint: The subject and body in E01 and E04 agree.

questions.prompt: SPF, DKIM and DMARC all pass. What does that establish?
options: The lookalike sender domain authenticated, but the message can still be phishing
questions.answer: The lookalike sender domain authenticated, but the message can still be phishing
questions.hint: E03 authenticates the sending domain; E06 compares it with the official domain.

questions.prompt: Which extracted file should you seek in endpoint logs?
questions.hint: E05 names the script inside the ZIP.

questions.prompt: For the carried C2 IP, what is the interval between its four small flows? Answer in seconds.
questions.hint: Filter by the C2 destination and subtract consecutive small-flow times. The 30-second telemetry pattern belongs to another host.

questions.prompt: For the carried C2 IP, how many KiB left in its two bulk outbound flows? Answer in KiB.

model.summary: A fake VPN certificate update reached Maya Chen. The extracted JavaScript ran on ISU-LT-042, launched PowerShell, installed an at-logon task and contacted 198.51.100.42. TLS flow records show about 512 KiB of outbound payload; they do not reveal its contents. From the same host, an RC4 service ticket request preceded the first observed svc-vpn-backup logon and an unauthorized VPN-Admins change.
model.affected: ISU\mchen; ISU\svc-vpn-backup; ISU-LT-042 (192.0.2.42). Investigate DC-01 activity; no evidence here proves DC-01 itself is compromised.
model.indicators: VPN-Cert-Update.zip; VPN-Cert-Update.js; 6e9e6b8ffb8c29a258ba2e37df1461fa896675e682d593af13b6d4b579207a92; sync.isu-support.example.com; 198.51.100.42; ISU VPN Update task.
model.containment: Isolate ISU-LT-042; disable or reset ISU\mchen and ISU\svc-vpn-backup after preserving evidence; remove unauthorized VPN-Admins membership and scheduled task; block C2; scope mailbox delivery, other host connections and account activity. The RC4 4769 request before the first service-account logon is consistent with Kerberoasting, but ticket cracking and credential theft are inferred rather than directly observed. Verify outbound data contents before claiming which records left.
model.timeline: 09:02 email to Maya Chen; 09:05 script launched on ISU-LT-042 and C2 began; 09:06 at-logon task created; 09:08 RC4 service ticket request; 09:10 about 512 KiB outbound to C2; 09:11 unauthorized VPN-Admins membership change and first observed svc-vpn-backup logon from the laptop.
